questions.prompt: Which part of a method declaration is optional?
questions.explanation: Parameters are optional. A method can be declared with empty parentheses or no parentheses at all if it takes no arguments.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: _____ Multiply(int x, int y) { return x * y; }
questions.template: _____ Multiply(int x, int y) { return x * y; }

questions.prompt: Arrange the pieces of the method declaration: public int Add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }

options: The method name plus parameter types
questions.explanation: A method signature consists of the method name and the types of its parameters (not the return type).

Write a method named IsEven that takes an int and returns true if it is even. Call it with 4 and print the result.
When does a method's code start executing?
questions.explanation: Method code runs only when the method is called. Definition alone does not execute it.

Can two methods in the same class have the same name?
options: Yes, if they have different parameter types
Yes, if one is static and one is not
questions.explanation: Method overloading allows multiple methods with the same name as long as their parameter lists differ.
